name: Scott Eckhard Jewett

items.why: The item itself says no foreign-government payments, foreign-agent donors or similar ties were found, so there is no conduct to weigh under the foreign-ties criterion.

for_review: Item 1 has nothing behind it, and my search turned up no foreign-ties evidence. One search on the owner's sites (alexjoneslive.com, stewpeters.com, ryandawson.org, infowars.com) found nothing about this candidate. Check one lead I couldn't open: California's Department of Financial Protection and Innovation (DFPI) has an enforcement file on 'Scott Jewett' and Sweet Assets Franchise Group, Inc. (dba Donut Bar). It includes a June 29, 2020 citation and desist-and-refrain order, and a September 21, 2020 settlement dated and signed with a Boca Raton, FL address. Search snippets say Jewett was CEO and director of Sweet Assets. They also say the citation covered failing to promptly amend a franchise disclosure document and a willful violation of Corporations Code section 31200. The DFPI PDFs and file page would not load, so I couldn't read the order, the penalty or Jewett's response. I also couldn't confirm that this is the same Scott Jewett, though the Boca Raton address and his franchise-executive background suggest it. His campaign bio says he acquired the Pinspiration franchise concept in 2018. If it is the same man, it could count as an official finding that he filed misleading or late franchise disclosures. That would be a minor weight-1 filing violation under criterion 6, or possibly a weight-2 'lying about record' matter, depending on the wording. Read the DFPI documents before using it. Also, the Libertarian Party national page says he has 'a decade of government experience'. Other sources call this his first run for public office and describe him only as a businessman. Check what that phrase means.
